title: Body Burden of Dichlorodiphenyl Dichloroethene (DDE) and Childhood Pulmonary Function.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected via blood samples, pulmonary function tests, and self-administered questionnaires from a primary cohort of school children in Hesse, Germany.
summary: Longitudinal study assessing the association between blood DDE levels and pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1) in children aged 8-10 years, examining mediation by height and weight.
key_findings: Linear mixed models showed no significant associations between DDE and pulmonary function parameters after adjustment.
Path analysis demonstrated DDE at age 8 had significant inverse indirect and total effects on FVC at age 10 (−0.18 L per µg/L) and FEV1 at age 10 (−0.17 L per µg/L), mediated by height and weight.
DDE had negative total effects on height (−0.28 cm per µg/L) and weight (−0.24 kg per µg/L).
Sex-stratified analyses showed significant indirect negative effects of DDE on FVC (−0.25 L/µg/L in females, −0.21 L/µg/L in males) and FEV1 (−0.24 L/µg/L in females, −0.19 L/µg/L in males).
study_design: Longitudinal cohort study with repeated measurements and structural equation modeling (path analysis)
data_source_type: Primary cohort study / field data collection
population: Children aged 8-10 years in Hesse, Germany (n=328-344 with complete DDE and PFT data)
exposure_domain: Persistent organic pollutants / organochlorines (DDE blood levels)
limitations: DDE exposure not measured at age 9 years (values carried forward from age 8)
Reduced statistical power in sex-stratified analyses due to smaller sample sizes
Potential residual confounding from unmeasured immune markers or other environmental factors
